title: Austin's Future: Parks, Streets, Traffic
summary:
*   **New East Austin Park Discussion:** The Council met with a community committee to explore three potential sites (23-40 acres) for a new district park in East Austin, seeking further community input.
*   **Street Improvement Contract:** A $5,357.76 contract was awarded for grading and paving improvements on Anderson Lane, Guadalupe Street, and Purnell Drive.
*   **Lamar Boulevard Underpass:** Preliminary plans were reviewed for a significant underpass and traffic interchange project on Lamar Boulevard, with the city aiming to collaborate with state and railroad authorities for rapid development.

3:00 P. M.
Council Chamber, City Hall
The meeting was called to order with Mayor Miller presiding. Roll call: Present:
CouncilmenLong, Palmer, Pearson, White, Mayor Miller Absent:
None
Present also: W. T. Williams, Jr., City Manager; Doren R. Eskew, City Attorney; Reuben
Rountree, Jr., Director of Public Works; Beverly Sheffield, Recreation Director.
Members of the East Austin Committee present were Mrs. Estella White, Mrs. Howard McCall,
Mrs. Josephine Alexander, Mrs. Johnnie Y. Rice, and Mrs. Johnnie Mae Franklin.
The Mayor announced this was a special meeting for the purpose of meeting with a committee
from East Austin regarding a District Park; for considering the bids on Contract No.
57-C-36, and to discuss the plans for an underpass on Lamar
Boulevard at Third Street.
The City Manager and Director of Recreation presented aerial maps of three tracts of land
available for a park in this area. Tract I contained approximately 40 acres and is located
on East 12th Street extending south to Oak Springs Drive and bounded on the east by
Springdale Road and Webberville Road. Tract II contained approximately 23 acres and is
located on the south side of East 19th Street, south to East 12th Street from Airport
Boulevard to Redwood Street. Tract III contained approximately 28 acres and is located
south of Heflin Drive between Springdale Road and Webberville Road, being north of Simms
School.
Discussion was held and the Committee stated they would like to look at these tracts of
land and take this information back to their group and they would let the Council hear
from them as soon as possible. 512

interchange on Lamar Boulevard from 5th Street south to the Lamar Bridge. The plans were
discussed and the Mayor stated the city would work with the Highway Department and
Railroad and proceed as rapidly as possible to build this underpass.
